table.ruleA: Add the cycle's input to each stage's charge; rated charge not enforced
table.ruleB: Add the cycle's inflow to each tank; volume not enforced

table.ruleA: Stages 1 to 6 in strict order; excess over rated charge is added to stage n+1 before n+1 is handled (cascades); stage set to rated; stage 6 excess to ground; equal-to-rated does nothing
table.ruleB: Tanks 1 to 6 in order; excess over volume added to tank n+1 before n+1 is handled (cascades); tank set to volume; tank 6 excess to outfall; equal-to-volume does nothing

table.ruleA: Read charge after Step 2. CLEAR and charge >= upper mark -> ASSERTED; ASSERTED and charge <= lower mark -> CLEAR; otherwise unchanged; log (cycle, stage, before, after); at most one change per cycle
table.ruleB: Read contents after Step 2. STEADY and contents >= upper mark -> OVERLOADED; OVERLOADED and contents <= lower mark -> STEADY; otherwise unchanged; log (cycle, tank, before, after); at most one change per cycle

table.ruleA: All six amounts computed from charge at start of step using post-Step-3 state (CLEAR floor(q/4), ASSERTED floor(q/2)), then applied simultaneously; CLEAR amount to ground; ASSERTED amount to stage n-1 (stage 1 ASSERTED to ground); rated not enforced
table.ruleB: All six amounts computed from contents at start of step using post-Step-3 state (STEADY floor(q/4), OVERLOADED floor(q/2)), then applied simultaneously; STEADY amount to outfall; OVERLOADED amount to tank n-1 (tank 1 to outfall); volume not enforced

table.ruleA: If total of all six > 38 (strict; 38 does not trip), EVERY stage's charge becomes floor(q/2); removed charge to ground; log cycle
table.ruleB: If total of all six > 38 (strict; 38 does not trip), only OVERLOADED tanks become floor(q/2); STEADY tanks are left unchanged; removed liquor to outfall; log cycle
table.difference: Scope of the halving: A halves all six stages regardless of state; B halves only tanks in the OVERLOADED state (the analogue of ASSERTED), leaving STEADY/CLEAR tanks untouched. Trigger (strictly above 38) and destination (ground/outfall) are identical.

table.ruleA: (a) end charges 1-6, (b) end states, (c) all state changes in order occurred, (d) breaker-trip cycles, (e) ground total, (f) balance check start+inputs = end+ground
table.ruleB: (a) end contents 1-6, (b) end states, (c) all state changes (order not explicitly stated, but logged as they occur), (d) storm-bypass cycles, (e) outfall total, (f) balance check start+inflows = end+outfall
table.difference: Only cosmetic: B does not explicitly say 'in the order they occurred' for (c); content of the report is the same.
